header_summary:
A comprehensive framework of five Bitcoin Improvement Proposals—collectively defining Tapleaf 0xc2—proposes restoring and expanding Bitcoin Script capabilities, including re-enabling previously disabled opcodes, enabling transaction introspection, and supporting advanced primitives such as reusable macros. These updates, described in [BIP 440](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0440.mediawiki), [BIP 441](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0441.mediawiki), [OP_TX](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-unknown-optx.md), [Extended Primitives](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-unknown-extended-primitives.md), and [Reusable Macros](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-unknown-reusable-macros.md), introduce a computational budget for scripts to ensure validation costs remain bounded while preserving backward compatibility with existing address types. The reference implementation and benchmarking resources are available in a [dedicated Bitcoin Core fork](https://github.com/bitcoin-gsr/bitcoin/tree/gsr), supporting robust static analysis and safe deployment via a single soft fork.

To mitigate risks of seed exfiltration from malicious signing devices, an anti-exfiltration protocol has been drafted by Sjors Provoost and others, specifying collaborative nonce generation and new PSBT fields for enhanced security. This protocol, described at [https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil](https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil), has experimental support across multiple hardware wallets, though it remains unaudited and subject to further review and testing.

A critical vulnerability in Eclair 0.14.0 allowed attackers to exhaust node memory through improperly validated `start_batch` messages, potentially causing recurring Lightning Network node crashes and loss of funds. The flaw, rooted in deviations from [BOLT 2](https://github.com/lightning/bolts/blob/191462825ae341f0a27098765c075f01ca9bc6c2/02-peer-protocol.md?plain=1L3043) requirements, was resolved in [version 0.14.1](https://github.com/ACINQ/eclair/blob/d769db070424ae0ab6c05975fd7c86dac8b3e1f4/docs/release-notes/eclair-v0.14.1.md), and immediate upgrades are strongly advised.

Serialization strategies for policy objects are being debated, with a hybrid of TLV (for policy identifiers) and JSON (for human readability) emerging as a likely compromise to balance strict protocol requirements and reviewability. This approach, as discussed in [BIP draft deliberations](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bip-draft-co-signer-spending-policies/2955/7), aims to ensure compatibility across Lightning, DLC, and co-signer applications.

Wallet teams continue to confront compatibility challenges between Taproot (bc1p…) and SegWit (bc1q…) address formats, as service-side support for Taproot remains inconsistent. User experience considerations and ecosystem transparency are driving calls for improved resources such as a [compatibility database](https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Bech32_adoption) to better inform wallet development and end users.

recent_posts.title: [Proposal] Tapleaf 0xc2: An overview of the Great Script Restoration (GSR)
recent_posts.summary: - Five proposals introduce Tapleaf 0xc2, expanding Bitcoin Script functionality while maintaining backward compatibility.  - Advanced features like general covenants, transaction introspection, and reusable macros are now supported.  - Static analysis, strict execution limits, and benchmarking ensure safety, with open questions on broader impacts.

recent_posts.title: Draft BIPs: anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA, with PSBT fields
recent_posts.summary: - A protocol enables host systems to help generate nonces, reducing risks of seed exfiltration.  - Two BIP drafts define the protocol, introduce new PSBT fields, and detail compliance handling procedures.  - Formal cryptographic review is pending, with peer feedback and expert evaluation actively encouraged.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: Memory-exhaustion DoS in Eclair 0.14.0
recent_posts.summary: - Eclair 0.14.0 allowed attackers to exhaust node memory, causing denial-of-service by abusing batch parameters.  - Improper validation of batch size and channel IDs enabled unbounded message buffering and memory usage.  - The issue was fixed in version 0.14.1, and users should upgrade immediately for security.

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
recent_posts.summary: - Multiple serialization formats are being compared, each with unique trade-offs for policy object encoding.  - TLV, canonical JSON, and CBOR offer different compatibilities, readability, and challenges regarding field handling.  - There is a preference for a hybrid model, but feedback on failure cases and compatibility is requested.

recent_posts.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
recent_posts.summary: - Cryptocurrency wallet users often face compatibility issues when sending funds due to unsupported address formats.  - Wallet providers must balance future-proofing with current compatibility when choosing default address formats.  - Improved UI/UX and clear community resources are needed to help users address compatibility challenges efficiently.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary:
- The `staletip` proposal introduces an optional messaging system for sharing stale block tip information.
- Its technical policy limits messages to relevant tips, compressed headers, and maintains a recent tip cache.
- This initiative aims to enhance network observability, enabling improved diagnostics and response to stale events.

active_posts.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts.summary: - The draft proposes a standardized enforcement policy format to improve interoperability among blockchain security products.  - It includes various verification methods, enforces script-inclusion of all conditions, and supports Discreet Log Contracts.  - Feedback is requested on serialization formats, blinded verification feasibility, attestation formats, output language, and timelock requirements.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Quantum-safe output types and enforced collateralization aim to safeguard legacy cryptocurrency against quantum threats.  - Game-theoretic mechanisms like Quantum Landmines and auctions incentivize defenders and penalize potential attackers.  - These adaptive, incentive-driven protocols harness economic theory to strengthen security in decentralized systems.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal addresses vulnerabilities in Bitcoin’s protocol, including timewarp and merkle root computation risks.  - It recommends limits on legacy transaction types and invites community collaboration for further improvements.  - Some suggestions, like block size reduction, face debate due to concerns about scalability and protocol changes.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - Compact block reconstruction efficiency depends on node transaction awareness and changes to configuration settings.  - Increased inbound connections and mempool activity influence block reconstruction rates and associated request frequencies.  - Enabling `mempoolfullrbf` and evaluating connectivity models may optimize block propagation across the network.

active_posts.title: Public key recovery for EC leaves in P2MR (BIP-360)
active_posts.summary:
- The proposal enables public key recovery from elliptic curve signatures, reducing witness size without increasing quantum risk.
- The approach modifies signature validation, incorporates the root hash into challenges, and streamlines the witness structure.
- Revised nonce derivation enhances security, while blockchain space and transaction costs are efficiently minimized.

today_in_history_posts.title: Bitcoin Archaeology
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The author aims to rebuild early Bitcoin versions using MinGW, as Visual C++ 6 is unavailable.  - OpenSSL fails to build due to mk1mf.pl issues, likely caused by an incompatible MSYS perl version.  - Possible solutions include various build environments, patching, or precompiled releases, but difficulties persist.

today_in_history_posts.title: SIGHASH_SINGLE + update_fee Considered Harmful
today_in_history_posts.summary: - A vulnerability enables attackers to bypass penalties on HTLC transactions by redirecting inflated fees.  - Countermeasures include tighter channel policies and adopting a scorched earth approach for justice transactions.  - Addressing this requires removing certain fee appliances and considering the impact on channel usability.

today_in_history_posts.title: P2share: how to turn any network (or testnet!) into a bitcoin miner
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The p2share network distributes bitcoin mining rewards by randomly selecting a single shareholder for each block.  - Shares are transferable, enabling miners to accumulate or trade them based on network rules and incentives.  - This model promotes fairness, efficiency, and decentralization while minimizing transaction bloat in bitcoin mining.
